the boundary layer growth on the surface of a spinning body in an incompressible flow is studied when the angular velocity of rotation of the body is expressed as a series in powers of the square root of time, t.

we found that the use of a boundary layer model to predict heat transfer rates for the spinning disk is not accurate, and that we were able to develop a model based on the Navier-Stokes equation to accurately predict heat transfer rates.
the boundary layer on a rotating sphere is thinner at small times and that it separates earlier than the boundary layer on an unrotating sphere.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the growth of the boundary layer on a body in spinning motion, when the outer flow is expressed in a power series of √t.
the development of a new method for the analysis of the boundary-layer flow past a spinning body of revolution.
the growth and development of a boundary layer on the surface of a rotating body.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of the spinning body to reduce the drag of the vehicle in the hypersonic regime is a viable concept.
the boundary layer theory is a useful and important tool for studying the flow of fluids over bodies, but that its application must be done carefully, and that it is not always valid.
the use of the spin parameter in the analysis of boundary layer flows on a spinning body has been found to be of great value.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the separation of the boundary layer occurs for the spinning body when the Reynolds number is greater than a critical value.
, the boundary layer growth on spinning bodies is a complex phenomenon and it is difficult to predict the boundary layer growth in the presence of spinning.
, the growth of boundary layer is not affected by the spinning motion of the body.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the growth of a boundary layer is not a simple function of the Reynolds number and the Prandtl number, as is commonly assumed.
the growth of the boundary layer is faster when the body is rotating than when it is not.
the separation point is not a constant, but depends on time.
